Master ir a + infinitive for plans and me gustaría for wishes
Practise using sería + adjective to justify a choice
Build sentences combining past (fui, me encantó) and future tenses
method_card.title: Holidays and Travel Plans
method_card.content:
This lesson covers holiday destinations, countries and how to talk about travel plans using the near future tense (ir a + infinitive) and the conditional (me gustaría + infinitive).

SpanishEnglish
las vacacionesthe holidays
ir de vacacionesto go on holiday
viajarto travel
el viajethe journey / trip
la playathe beach
las montañasthe mountains
el campothe countryside
el extranjeroabroad
el verano pasadolast summer
el año que vienenext year
me encantóI loved it
me lo pasé bienI had a good time
me gustaríaI would like
voy a + infinitiveI am going to…
sería emocionanteit would be exciting

Grammar focus — near future and conditional: Use ir a + infinitive for plans you have already made: voy a ir a España (I am going to go to Spain). Use me gustaría + infinitive for wishes: me gustaría visitar México (I would like to visit Mexico). Use sería + adjective for hypotheticals: sería relajante (it would be relaxing). Note the preposition: ir a Francia (to France — motion), estar en Francia (in France — location).

Model paragraph: Este verano voy a ir de vacaciones a Italia con mi familia. Me gustaría visitar Roma porque sería muy interesante. El año pasado fui a la playa y me lo pasé muy bien. (This summer I am going to go on holiday to Italy with my family. I would like to visit Rome because it would be very interesting. Last year I went to the beach and I had a great time.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — holiday plans appear in every exam series

gold.source_text: Last summer I travelled to the countryside with my family. I swam in the river and I loved it. Next year I would like to visit Italy because it would be exciting.
model_answers: El verano pasado viajé al campo con mi familia. Nadé en el río y me encantó. El año que viene me gustaría visitar Italia porque sería emocionante.

steps: Learn the key preterite forms for holiday verbs: fui, visité, comí, hice, nadé
Master the imperfect for descriptions: era, hacía, había, estaba
Practise the contrast — preterite for events, imperfect for background
Build extended narratives combining both tenses with connectives
method_card.title: Past Holidays and Experiences
method_card.content:
This lesson is the central grammar challenge of Theme 6: the contrast between the preterite and the imperfect tense. Spanish requires both in a past holiday narrative — unlike French, which collapses both into a single perfect tense.

SpanishEnglish
fui (preterite of ir)I went
visité (preterite of visitar)I visited
comí (preterite of comer)I ate
nadé (preterite of nadar)I swam
hice (preterite of hacer)I did / I made
era (imperfect of ser)it was (description)
hacía sol / calor / fríoit was sunny / hot / cold
había (imperfect of haber)there was / there were
se veían (imperfect of verse)you could see (description)
me lo pasé genialI had a brilliant time
fue increíbleit was incredible
sin embargohowever
ademásalso / moreover

Grammar focus — preterite vs imperfect: Use the preterite for completed, single events: fui a Roma (I went to Rome), comí pizza (I ate pizza). Use the imperfect for descriptions, ongoing background, or repeated past actions: el hotel era bonito (the hotel was nice), hacía calor todos los días (it was hot every day). Both tenses often appear together: Estaba en la playa cuando empezó a llover (I was on the beach when it started to rain) — the ongoing background uses the imperfect; the sudden interruption uses the preterite.

Model paragraph: El verano pasado fui de vacaciones a Portugal con mi familia. El hotel era muy cómodo y hacía sol todos los días. Visité varios monumentos y comí mucho marisco. Sin embargo, un día perdí mi móvil — ¡fue un desastre! (Last summer I went on holiday to Portugal with my family. The hotel was very comfortable and it was sunny every day. I visited several monuments and ate a lot of seafood. However, one day I lost my mobile — it was a disaster!)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — past holiday narratives appear in every writing and speaking series

Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences about grammar accuracy","improvement":"optional specific correction"}

method_card.title: Accommodation and Hotel Stays
method_card.content:
This lesson covers hotel and campsite vocabulary, booking accommodation, describing what it was like, and dealing with problems — all of which appear in speaking role-plays and writing tasks.

SpanishEnglish

una habitación doblea double room

Grammar focus — quisiera and the preterite/imperfect for accommodation: Use quisiera (I would like) for polite booking requests: quisiera reservar una habitación doble. Use the preterite for the action of staying: me alojé en un hotel (I stayed in a hotel). Use the imperfect for descriptions of what it was like: era cómodo (it was comfortable), tenía piscina (it had a pool). The key distinction: me alojé (I stayed — single completed action, preterite) vs era grande (it was big — ongoing description, imperfect).

Model paragraph: Me alojé en un hotel de cuatro estrellas cerca del centro. La habitación era grande y tenía vistas al mar. Sin embargo, no funcionaba el aire acondicionado, así que pedí cambiar de habitación. (I stayed in a four-star hotel near the centre. The room was big and had sea views. method_card.content:
This lesson combines two common exam topics: visiting tourist attractions and ordering in a restaurant. Both require the preterite for completed past actions and polite request forms for the speaking exam.

SpanishEnglish

Grammar focus — preterite for events and polite usted forms: Use the preterite for completed past actions when describing your sightseeing or meal: visité el castillo (I visited the castle), comí paella (I ate paella). Note: estaba delicioso uses the imperfect for the description of taste (ongoing quality). When complaining to a waiter, use the usted form: Perdone (Excuse me — usted, formal), ¿Puede traer…? (Can you bring…?). Do NOT use Perdona (informal) or ¿Puedes? (informal) in a restaurant role-play.

Model paragraph: Ayer visité la catedral y el museo de arte. Por la noche fui a un restaurante con mi familia. Pedí el pollo con arroz y la comida estaba muy rica. Sin embargo, el servicio fue un poco lento. (Yesterday I visited the cathedral and the art museum. In the evening I went to a restaurant with my family. I ordered the chicken with rice and the food was very tasty. However, the service was a bit slow.)

method_card.title: Weather, Travel Problems and Transactions
method_card.content:
This lesson covers weather vocabulary, travel problems and transactional language at a tourist information office — all of which are tested across speaking, listening, reading and writing papers.

SpanishEnglish
Hace solIt's sunny
Hace calorIt's hot
Hace fríoIt's cold
Hace buen tiempoThe weather is good
Hace mal tiempoThe weather is bad
Llueve / Está lloviendoIt's raining
Nieva / Está nevandoIt's snowing
Está nubladoIt's cloudy
He perdido mi maleta.I have lost my suitcase.
Me han robado.I have been robbed.
He perdido mi pasaporte.I have lost my passport.
¿Dónde está…?Where is…?
¿A qué hora abre/cierra?What time does it open/close?
¿Puede recomendarme…?Can you recommend…? (formal)

Grammar focus — weather expressions and the perfect tense for travel problems: Weather in Spanish uses hacer + noun: hace calor (literally 'it makes heat'). In the past, use the imperfect for background weather description: hacía mucho frío (it was very cold). For travel problems, the perfect tense (haber + past participle) is natural for recent or ongoing relevance: he perdido mi pasaporte (I have lost my passport). Polite requests at tourist information use ¿Puede…? (Can you…? — usted form).

Model paragraph: Ayer hacía mucho viento y llovía. Por la tarde fui a la oficina de turismo porque he perdido mi pasaporte. El empleado me ayudó y me recomendó una comisaría cerca del centro. (Yesterday it was very windy and it was raining. In the afternoon I went to the tourist information office because I had lost my passport. The employee helped me and recommended a police station near the centre.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — weather and travel problems appear across all papers

Check: imperfect for weather (hacía), preterite for single events (nadé, empezó), past continuous (estaba tomando), conditional (me gustaría, haría). Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences about grammar accuracy","improvement":"optional specific correction"}

gaps.rule: Present subjunctive after es importante que

wrong.cuidar: cuidar is the infinitive. You need a conjugated subjunctive form after es importante que.
wrong.cuidamos: cuidamos is the present indicative (we look after). After es importante que, the subjunctive is required: cuidemos.

gaps.correct_explain: cuidemos is the nosotros present subjunctive of cuidar. After es importante que, Spanish requires the subjunctive.

gaps.rule: Present subjunctive of poder after para que

wrong.poder: poder is the infinitive. You need a conjugated subjunctive form after para que.
wrong.pueden: pueden is the present indicative. After para que, use the subjunctive: puedan.

gaps.correct_explain: puedan is the ellos/ellas present subjunctive of poder. After para que, the subjunctive is required.

bronze.question: Match the Spanish weather expressions to their English meaning
Match the Spanish to the English meaning

wrong.hace: hace is the present tense. Ayer requires a past tense.
wrong.har\u00e1: hará is the future tense. Ayer is past.

gaps.correct_explain: hacía (imperfect) is used for weather descriptions in the past. Hizo (preterite) is also accepted.

wrong.nadaba: nadaba is the imperfect — for habitual past actions, not a single event yesterday.

gaps.correct_explain: nadé is the yo preterite of nadar — a completed action yesterday.

sentence_parts: en el mar con mis amigos.

gaps.rule: Perfect tense — past participle of perder

wrong.perd\u00ed: perdí is the preterite (I lost). Both are possible, but he perdido (perfect) is more natural for an ongoing problem.
wrong.pierde: pierde is the present tense (loses/is losing). This is a past event.

gaps.correct_explain: perdido is the past participle of perder. He perdido = I have lost (perfect tense).

wrong.Descans\u00e9: Descansé is the preterite (I rested). The English says 'I was resting' — an ongoing background action, so use the past continuous.

gaps.correct_explain: Estaba descansando = I was resting. Past continuous: estar in the imperfect + gerund (-ando for -ar verbs).

wrong.empezaba: empezaba is the imperfect. The interrupting action (it started to rain) is a single, sudden event → preterite.

gaps.correct_explain: Empezó is the preterite of empezar — a sudden interrupting event.

silver.question: Complete the sentence
Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Ayer hizo sol y estaba nadado en el mar.
silver.explanation: The past continuous uses the gerund (-ando/-iendo), not the past participle (-ado/-ido). Nadar → nadando (swimming), not nadado (swum — past participle).

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Hacía calor — note hacía is imperfect (ongoing description of heat). It was hot.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Ayer (yesterday) signals the past. Weather in the past is described with the imperfect.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Hacer in the imperfect (3rd person singular) = hacía. Llover (to rain) in the imperfect = llovía.

steps.label: Answer
